Yes. 

The ending feels completely natural, earned, and purposeful. Throughout the story, the central conflict is the unspoken tension of what will happen "after" the six-week residency ends, as both characters are accustomed to living in temporary increments and avoiding permanent attachments. The climax on the mud flats forces them to finally confront this question. The conclusion ties up these thematic threads by showing a clear shift in their character arcs: Toby refers to a "next time" ("you watch the chart. I'll watch you") and drives away toward a job offer "he had not yet answered yes to," while the narrator writes "Boston, September" in a notebook explicitly kept for "things worth keeping." Rather than feeling abrupt, the ending arrives at the exact emotional resolution the entire narrative was building toward.
